steps.step: MN1 brute force (3 modes, random BdG ground state, three random BdG quadratics): <Q^2> = 1/4 Tr(AC)^2 + 1/2 Tr(ACAC^T) is exact, and 1/2 Psi^dag Sigma_K Psi (Sigma_K = tau_x B) is the exact first-order mean-field operator: d<H_int>/ds = d<1/2 Psi^dag Sigma_K Psi>/ds along a family of Gaussian ground states

MN2 Theta_1 one-loop structure (T = 0, BZ grids 24^3 / 36^3 / 48^3): Sigma^(1)(k) = f(k)^2 Sigma^rho with Sigma^rho = alpha 1 + b.sigma (x) 1_16, no anomalous part, alpha = 0 (particle-hole), b along [111] (C3); hence Sigma^(1)(Gamma) = O(k^4) and Sigma^(1)(P) = b.sigma (f(P) = 1)

MN3 the mirror node is SHIFTED, not gapped: the one-loop Hamiltonian h_W + f^2 b.sigma has an exact zero at P + dk with dk linear in g along [111], the old P is no longer a zero (|E(P)| = |b| g), the Weyl charge of the moved node stays -1 (Gamma: +1); Spin(10) x Z4 forbid every Majorana bilinear of one 16, so no translation-invariant bilinear can gap it
steps.detail: |dk|/g = [39.144, 38.36, 36.72] for g = 0.001 / 0.003 / 0.01 (linear prediction 39.582/t, approached for g -> 0; external estimate 80/t is a factor 2.02 larger -- normalisation here fixed by MN1 and by the frozen O_A of reweight.py); direction [0.5774, 0.5774, 0.5774]; |E(old P)| = 39.582 g; Weyl charges P -1.000, shifted node -1.000, Gamma +1.000

steps.step: MN4 QMC comparison (16 sites, beta = 2): the one-loop Hamiltonian h_W + g f^2 Sigma^rho(cell, beta) -- a pure node shift, no mass -- explains the major part (70-115 %) of the measured depletion 1/2 - G_P(beta/2) at g = 0.003, 0.01, 0.03; the remainder (beyond one loop, multiplet splitting or a genuine gap) cannot be resolved at the old P -> node tracking needed
steps.detail: g = 0.003: one-loop 0.4969 vs QMC 0.4965+-0.0001 (one-loop share 89 %); g = 0.01: one-loop 0.4671 vs QMC 0.4582+-0.0008 (one-loop share 79 %); g = 0.03: one-loop 0.2952 vs QMC 0.2441+-0.0071 (one-loop share 80 %); cell/beta Sigma^rho: b/g = [21.529, 21.529, 21.529], alpha/g = 8.9e-15

steps.step: MN6 flavour-twisted boundary conditions (Spin(10) Cartan Sigma_12 = 1/2 - n_0, the only continuous twist compatible with H_int, which conserves charge only mod 4): a reciprocal-superlattice twist reproduces the untwisted Hamiltonian and pairing matrix exactly; the ten channels rotate real-orthogonally (sum O_A^2 invariant); the free twisted spectrum of the Q = +-1/2 flavours is h_W(k +- delta); the filtered local correlators of the twisted cell are site-independent (translation covariance of the twisted interaction)
steps.detail: trivial-twist deviation 1.6e-16; channel rotation residual 1.1e-16 (R real orthogonal: True); twisted spectrum error 1.2e-14; local correlator site dependence 2.8e-15

steps.step: MN7 32-site points: the pure finite-size multiplet picture (G_P depends only on g/N; test 32 sites, beta = 2, g = 0.02 vs 16 sites, g = 0.01) is excluded, and the one-loop node shift explains the 32-site depletion almost completely, i.e. the beyond-one-loop residual of the 16-site cell shrinks with volume (16 and 32 are not homothetic: indication, not a scaling law)
steps.detail: 32 sites beta = 2.0, g = 0.02: QMC 0.3817+-0.0010, one-loop 0.3838, share 98 %; 32 sites beta = 2.5, g = 0.01: QMC 0.4473+-0.0002, one-loop 0.4465, share 101 %; 32 sites beta = 2.5, g = 0.03: QMC 0.2192+-0.0060, one-loop 0.2216, share 99 %; 16 sites beta = 2, g = 0.01: QMC 0.4582 (multiplet prediction for 32/0.02: equal), one-loop share 79 %

steps.step: MN8 one-loop node trajectory along [111] (the C3 axis; total charge of the one-loop band structure is 0): Gamma stays a fixed +1 node for every g; a -1 mirror node exists for every g; it moves continuously up to g ~ 0.020, then a +-1 pair is created on the axis, the new +1 annihilates the old mirror and the new -1 carries the mirror charge on (pair window g ~ 0.0205 ... 0.0235) -> the linear regime ends near g ~ 0.02 and the mirror charge is never removed at first order (off-axis pairs appear around g = 0.05, global census)

MN5 (statement) Gate B criterion corrected: Delta(P) > 0 at the old P does not show a mirror gap (it is reproduced by node motion); required is min_{k != Gamma} Delta_odd(k) > 0 with node tracking (twisted boundary conditions, k_star(g, V), Delta(k_star)), plus Gamma Weyl intact, all independent mirror composites gapped, Spin(10) x Z4 x translations unbroken; a genuine mirror removal must be non-perturbative (no bilinear can gap a single Weyl node; Green-function zeros are the candidate mechanism)
